meta.note: The evidence base behind this platform. Every source below was read and analyzed, not merely listed — each entry carries what we took from it. Official documents, Thailand's national corpus, and an independent 14-dimension research synthesis.

items.title: ASCN Concept Note
items.takeaway: Establishes the network as a cooperative platform with three objectives — facilitate cooperation, catalyse bankable projects, secure external-partner funding. The 'people-first, technology-as-enabler' frame originates here.

items.title: ASEAN Smart Cities Framework
items.takeaway: The non-binding guide: three strategic outcomes, two urban systems, six focus areas, two enablers. Deliberately a guide, not a mandate — the structural reason ASCN coordinates rather than commands.

items.title: East Asia Summit Leaders' Statement on ASEAN Smart Cities
items.takeaway: Heads of State of ASEAN plus Australia, China, India, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, Russia and the US endorsed the network on 15 November 2018 — the political basis for the eight-partner cooperation ecosystem.

items.title: Consolidated Smart City Action Plans (SCAPs)
items.takeaway: The priority areas and action plans of the 26 pilot cities, self-defined by each city — the original source of the project portfolio and its uneven, locally-owned character.

items.title: ASCN Terms of Reference & M&E Framework — adoption
items.takeaway: The 22–24 August 2019 meeting where the ASCN Terms of Reference and the Monitoring & Evaluation Framework were adopted — the procedural birth of the annual reporting cycle this platform reads.

items.title: ASCN M&E Report 2022
items.takeaway: The baseline: a 77-project portfolio across the roster, the first consolidated read of network-wide implementation.

items.title: ASCN M&E Report 2023
items.takeaway: Second cycle — roster and portfolio growth; investment framing sharpens under Indonesia's shepherdship.

items.title: ASCN M&E Report 2024
items.takeaway: Portfolio reaches 108 projects; the financing toolkit and ASUF activity mature.

items.title: ASCN M&E Report 2025 (as of 30 Sep 2025)
items.takeaway: 134 projects, 81% ongoing — the primary appendix source for this platform's project database. Confirms the method counts projects, not outcomes.

items.title: ASCN under Singapore's Chairmanship
items.takeaway: Founding-year activities and the handover into the Shepherd model — Singapore's institutional design for surviving annual chair rotation.

items.title: ASCN 2019: Advancing Partnership for Sustainability
items.source: DEPA / Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, Thailand
items.takeaway: Thailand's chairmanship-year report, edited by DEPA leadership — the clearest record of Thailand's organising role and the partnership-for-sustainability theme.

items.title: ASCN 2019 Report (rev.02)
items.takeaway: The detailed editorial record of the Thai chair year — confirms Thailand's early, hands-on stewardship of the network's operational machinery.

items.title: Cabinet Resolution on the ASCN Progress Report
items.source: Cabinet of Thailand (มติ ครม. 29 ต.ค. 2562)
items.takeaway: ASCN reporting reached Thailand's Cabinet on 29 October 2019 — evidence the network was treated as national policy, not a side initiative.

items.title: ASEAN Smart City Planning Guidebook
items.takeaway: The shared planning methodology offered to member cities — useful, but a single template applied across radically different cities, which is exactly where local judgement has to take over.

items.title: MLIT ASEAN Smart City Planning Guidebook (Draft Final)
items.takeaway: Japan's draft methodology submitted for ASCN consideration — a case study in how a partner's framework becomes regional practice, and why it needs local adaptation rather than wholesale adoption.

items.title: Smart City Handbook: Thailand
items.takeaway: DEPA's national playbook — the most developed of any ASCN member, including the Thai Smart City Index that already does the outcome-level measurement the regional M&E lacks.

items.title: Smart City Week 2020 — Proceedings (EN)
items.takeaway: Thailand's flagship convening of regional smart-city practice — demonstrates a model built on open exchange and showcase rather than vendor lock-in.

items.title: Smart City Week 2020 — Proceedings (TH)
items.takeaway: The Thai-language edition — evidence the work is built for its own public first, in its own language, not translated in from outside.

items.title: ASCN Contact List (as of 31 Jan 2026)
items.takeaway: National focal points and city representatives across all 38 cities — the human network behind the roster (personal details withheld from this public platform).

items.title: ASCN Representative / Ambassador details
items.takeaway: The designated city-level representatives — confirming who actually carries each city's participation between annual meetings.

groups.group: Independent research synthesis (this platform's own analysis)

items.title: ASCN Comprehensive Research Brief
items.takeaway: The synthesis spine: governance, projects, partnerships, financing, M&E, technology, transport, environment, academic critique, comparison, private sector, citizen impact, future outlook, and data sources — distilled into the data layer you are reading.

items.title: 14 research dimensions + cross-verification + insight notes
items.takeaway: Each dimension independently investigated and cross-verified, then reconciled against the official record — the working papers behind every claim on this site, available on request.
